per_object_cap.stated: Packages larger than 150 MB or single files larger than 20 MB (in the case of GitHub) are not supported by default. We recommend removing files that are not needed from your package when possible. If you need to set a higher limit for your package, open an issue in this repo.
per_object_cap.notes: We actually allow files up to 20 MB for GitHub regardless of the overall repo size

retention.stated: Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion. We do not accept removal requests simply because a package or version was unpublished, deleted upstream, or is no longer needed.
retention.notes: We use a permanent S3 storage to ensure all files remain available even if GitHub goes down or a repository or a release is deleted by its author.

limits_note: 150 MB per npm package, 20 MB per single GitHub file (both default, raisable via GitHub issue). Rate limiting applies to purge, not to reads. Terms prohibit 'using jsDelivr CDN as a general-purpose file or media hosting service' and 'hosting videos, file backups, or other files in large quantities'. Enforcement is the technical risk, not the capability.

reliability_note: Retention is *stronger* than the origin: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion. We do not accept removal requests simply because a package or version was unpublished, deleted upstream, or is no longer needed.' Once a URL has been fetched it keeps working after you delete the npm package. That is a genuine cold-archive property. Counter-risk: a 150 MB package cap means a naive >150 MB npm tarball 403s ('Package size exceeded the configured limit of 150 MB') even though npm itself accepted it.

extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-09
extras.quota_verbatim: No storage quota of its own — it is a *serving and permanence* layer over npm and GitHub, so the quota is whatever the origin package holds. Hard limits: packages >150 MB and (for GitHub) single files >20 MB are refused by default, raisable on request.
extras.limits_verbatim: 150 MB per npm package, 20 MB per single GitHub file (both default, raisable via GitHub issue). Rate limiting applies to purge, not to reads. Terms prohibit 'using jsDelivr CDN as a general-purpose file or media hosting service' and 'hosting videos, file backups, or other files in large quantities' — enforcement is the technical risk, not the capability.
extras.egress_verbatim: Fully free and explicitly unmetered. Terms of Use (effective Oct 5, 2026), verbatim: 'using jsDelivr CDN is free for both personal and commercial use, there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests.' About page: 'There are no bandwidth limits or premium features and its completely free to use by anybody.'
extras.chaining_verbatim: Chains onto npm (see npm candidate) or onto GitHub repos: publish the blob as an npm tarball, then serve it from jsDelivr at a URL with 1-year immutable cache and no bandwidth charge. This upgrades any npm/GitHub bulk store from 'downloadable' to 'CDN-served with free egress', which is exactly the 1 TiB/day serving workload.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Plain GET on cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/<path> and /gh/<owner>/<repo>@<ref>/<path>. No client needed. Cache-purge API exists (email-gated).
extras.agent_focus: Package ecosystems as blob stores: npm, PyPI, crates.io, Maven Central, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist, Conda/conda-forge, Hex, Pub.dev, CocoaPods, R, CPAN, Hackage — per-artifact caps, version-unlimited behaviour, retention/deletion policy

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
